name: encode control, DEL, high and UTF-8 bytes
ref: cat -v notation (POSIX/GNU/BSD cat), output of cat -v checked on the sample bytes

name: encode non-ASCII UTF-8 e-acute (c3 a9)
ref: cat -v notation (POSIX/GNU/BSD cat), output of cat -v checked on the sample bytes (M-C M-))

example.title: UTF-8 bytes shown with M-
example.note: The letter é is two bytes, C3 and A9, shown as M-C and M-) (M- marks a byte above 127).

name: encode low control bytes 01 02 1f
ref: cat -v notation (POSIX/GNU/BSD cat), output of cat -v checked on the sample bytes (^A ^B ^_)

example.title: Control bytes as ^ letters
example.note: Bytes 01 to 1f become ^A to ^_, the letter being the byte plus 64.

name: encode every high-bit form (80 9f a0 fe)
ref: cat -v notation (POSIX/GNU/BSD cat), output of cat -v checked on the sample bytes (M-^@ M-^_ M-space M-~)

example.title: Bytes above 127 with M-
example.note: M- marks a byte with the high bit set: 80 is M- then ^@, the notation of 00.

name: decode the sample back to bytes
ref: cat -v notation (POSIX/GNU/BSD cat), output of cat -v checked on the sample bytes (inverse)

name: decode M- notation to UTF-8 e-acute
ref: cat -v notation (POSIX/GNU/BSD cat), output of cat -v checked on the sample bytes (inverse)

example.title: M- marks bytes above 127
example.note: M-C and M-) together give C3 and A9, which read as é.

name: decode ^^ is 0x1e and M-^^ is 0x9e
ref: cat -v notation (POSIX/GNU/BSD cat), output of cat -v checked on the sample bytes (^ + 0x5e)

name: decode M-M- is 0xcd then a hyphen
ref: cat -v notation (POSIX/GNU/BSD cat), output of cat -v checked on the sample bytes (M-M is 0xcd)

name: decode ^M before a hyphen is CR, not M-
ref: cat -v notation (POSIX/GNU/BSD cat), output of cat -v checked on the sample bytes (^M is 0x0d)

example.title: ^M is a carriage return
example.note: The ^M is the carriage return, 0d, and the hyphen after it is a plain character, not an M- mark.

example.title: Not every letter follows a caret
example.note: A caret is only read before a capital letter or a few symbols, so ^a is an error with E_COERCE.
